PC: Perform initial primary assessment of airway, breathing, circulation and disability
Identify concern for CVA and prioritizes acquisition of imaging
Perform assessment of patient with NIH stroke scale
Recognize abnormal vitals and change in mental status
Treat impending cerebral herniation with hyperosmolar therapy
Addresses blood pressure prior to administration of tPA
Requests access to an NIH stroke scale resource
Calculates NIH stroke scale independent of outside resources*
Orders CBC, BMP, INR and ECG
Selects appropriate anti-hypertensive agent prior to tPA
Identifies backup airway maneuver prior to intubation*
MK: Recognizes normal CT does not exclude ischemic stroke (family/nurse may ask if not apparent)
Considers differential for change in mental status following tPA
ICS: Discuss risks, benefits and alternatives of treatment
Request patient representative for family during decompensation
Provides family member with possible diagnoses
Concisely presents patient to admitting physician
